description: CO₂ emissions per person against GDP per person (PPP) for every country of a million people or more, from the World Bank, and the paths of six countries since 1990. Statistics idea: an elasticity is a slope on log–log axes. Least squares of ln CO₂ on ln GDP gives the % change in emissions per 1% of income across countries, with a t interval and R². Within countries the slope over time is different, negative for Sweden, the UK, Germany and the US: a slope between groups is not the relation within them (ecological fallacy), and neither is a cause. Caveats: territorial emissions (imports not counted), latest year per country, PPP GDP in constant 2021 dollars.
name: CO₂ and income: elasticity on log–log axes
